A punctual reissue of a rare Eye 4 Sound tech-acid house party starter from 2004, this Repeat version of Dexter's 'Paradox' stays faithful to one of many EPs in UK artist Mat Royall's regal flush of technical itches to last from 01 to 06, spread across labels like Beat Code, Random House and, in more recent years, Real Deal and Bosh Records. 'Paradox' is subset by the fun-loving 'Ychtm Acid' on the B-side, and while we can't claim to be so clever as to be able to decode this standout track's strange titular acronym, we can vouch for the sickness of its eccentric percussions and atmosphere, a fine case of what we call "mood design".

item.title: Chris Pascoe - Mong Juice / Trippy Breakfast
item.description: Label: Evasive Records | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: UK Tech House Reissue
item.content:encoded:
Label: Evasive Records

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: UK Tech House Reissue

Evasive repress seriesWe rewind to 2004, revisiting a quietly influential moment in the Evasive Records catalogue. Following earlier collaborations with Asad Rizvi and Haris, UK producer Chris Pascoe steps out solo with Mong Juice / Trippy Breakfast— a release that captured his deep, late-night take on tech house at the time. Cut with a strong musical sensibility — Pascoe is a skilled bass guitarist, a fact reflected in the record’s sub bass patterns crafting a rich, rolling low end — Mong Juice delivers a dubby, spacious groove driven by reverb-soaked textures and an old-school bleep techno bassline. On the flip, Trippy Breakfast leans into deeper, more tribal territory, pairing hypnotic rhythms with warm minor-key chords. Mixdown came courtesy of the late great Simon Copleston (Iteration X / Rob & Si) at Online Studios, Croydon where Si put his expert engineering touch to the sound of this record. Originally released in small quantities and favoured by selectors who valued subtlety over spectacle, this EP now returns as part of the Evasive repress series — a reminder of a sound built for long nights, locked grooves and dancefloors that reward patience.

Tracklist:

  • A1. Mong Juice
  • A2. Trippy Breakfast

Opener 'Your Touch' is one of his best ever to be honest - an effortlessly smooth cut with frayed edges, humid chords running through the middle and a simple but effective vocal sample full of soul. 'June' has more bounce and a hint of New York swing from the 90s while 'Your Touch' (Tuccillo dub mix) is a playful one for the early evening. The same Ibiza based producer offers a vocal mix of Them Blues that is great for sunny outdoor sessions.

Daniel Poli returns in Poli-phonic wax style, following up two 2025 remixes from last December of Timeless Banditz' 'House Down' and Mass G/Matt Thomas' 'Power Kill' respectively. Those set the tone for an ongoing collaboration between the longtime London underground rider and the still newly inaugural Slow-Wave label; now 'Sin Chronicities' delivers four killer originals from a preciously raw pioneer's perspective, bringing his irreplaceable frontier experience to new moves in the UK tech sound. Chicago house newcomer Arsene's 'Jack Shit' is guaranteed to detonate on impact, because its 7" release back in February has already done plenty of damage and got shouts from Luke Solomon, Moodymann and Danny Krivit among more. Now the Chicago upstart finally unleashes the full EP with three other, equally fresh cuts of raw, tracky Windy City house. Crunchy drum machines, hypnotic basslines and that unmistakable Chi-town swing are all present and correct here, with dark undertones but persuasive atmospheres all packed with Arsene's own urgent spark. No weak imitations here - this is a familiar analogue grit with future intent.

Star Creature really is one of our star labels right now. The Chicago outlet's next trick is to welcome back Arsene with a second 12" that centres his analogue house credentials. The NYC via Windy City producer moves beyond the raw punch of earlier cuts while locking into deeper East Coast sensibilities without losing that physical, club-ready clout. Each track is built on rugged drums and elastic basslines, always with a sense of movement. There's a toughness here, but also restraint, with grooves unfolding patiently rather than demanding attention outright. Arsene again shows he is one to keep an eye on.

The A-side of Parisian producer Serious A's label debut, 'Diagonal Wave', falls into this category. Propelled forwards by a lo-fi, mid-80s style Windy City drum machine rhythm, it sees her reach for undulating synthesiser melodies, TB-303 style bass and chords so deep and drowsy they could have been taken from a Mood Hut release. Over on side B, 'Songo Blu' is a more densely layered and immersive affair that blurs the boundaries between crackling early Chicago deep house, Damn Funk, lo-fi boogie beatmaker Onra and the usual Star Creature sound.

The Funkin' Machine are the latest hot property to come out of Italian city Naples, with the band's line-up including members of such celebrated outfits as Nu Genea and Mystic Jungle. You can hear some echoes of those acts across their debut album, Napoletanite - at least in their use of spacey jazz-funk synths, layered percussion and nods to Balearic boogie - but for the most part it's an insatiably funky, floor-focused affair that draws plenty from space-funk, psych-funk and the groover end of the Afro-cosmic spectrum. It's colourful, vibrant, urgent and hugely entertaining - a future classic whose timeless and colourful sound offers more than mere nostalgia for the late 70s and early 80s.

item.title: JS Edits - Jolene Cuts #2
item.description: Label: JS Edits 02 | Prix: 14,00 € | Style: House, Edit
item.content:encoded:

Prix: 14,00 €

Style: House, Edit

Jolene Cuts delivers a stunning 5-track vinyl-only release that reinvents the spirit of 90s French Touch for today’s dancefloors. No edits here—these are 100% original productions crafted by Danny & Mike, masters of filtered house grooves. From the funk-drenched “Without,” a Kool & The Gang-inspired house monster, to “Fall,” a euphoric blast reminiscent of the best Daft Punk moments, every cut is designed for maximum floor impact. “Mon ami Julien” dives deeper with a warm and hypnotic Scott Grooves vibe, while “Ready for Love” feels like Cerrone remixed by early Bob Sinclar at his peak—pure disco magic reimagined. The record closes with “Burning,” a banging, feel-good anthem built to ignite any set. This is a true celebration of filtered house, disco energy, and feel-good music—strictly vinyl, strictly limited, and packed with five undeniable club weapons. Perfect for DJs who want to tear the club apart, vinyl purists, and anyone who knows that real French Touch doesn’t need gimmicks—just groove, soul, and timeless dancefloor power. Once it’s gone, it’s gone.

  • B1.Mon ami Julien

item.title: Byron The Aquarius - O R G A S M A N I A
item.description: Label: Skylax extra series | Prix: 14,00 € | Style: House, Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Skylax extra series

Prix: 14,00 €

Style: House, Deep House

There are records that follow the rules, and others that rewrite them in real time. With O R G A S M A N I A, Byron The Aquarius returns to Skylax with a deeper, freer and more unpredictable statement — where jazz instinct meets raw machine funk, and structure dissolves into pure feeling. Rooted in the lineage of Detroit yet never confined by it, Byron operates in that rare zone where house music becomes expression rather than format. His sound doesn’t chase functionality — it breathes, it stretches, it resists. The EP opens with Back 2 Zion (Tomorrow), a spiritual and meditative journey built on loose drums and luminous chords, carrying a sense of elevation — early morning music where the dancefloor begins to think again. Enter the Co$mos (Fool) pushes further into abstraction, with drifting synths and broken rhythms unfolding in a non-linear structure, navigating between Sun Ra’s cosmic language and Detroit futurism. On the flip, Mr. Captain Crunchhh brings a raw, playful energy — crunchy textures, off-grid swing and an almost improvised groove, alive and unpredictable, a leftfield tool designed to disrupt expectations. Finally, O R G A S M A N I A stands as the centerpiece — hypnotic, sensual and immersive, locking into a deep repetitive groove while evolving in subtle layers, a late-night body experience guided by a sharp musical mind. Across four tracks, Byron The Aquarius confirms his unique position between jazz musician, house producer and sonic storyteller, with a trajectory spanning Sound Signature, Axis, Eglo, Apron and Shall Not Fade, continuing to resonate from Detroit to Berlin and beyond. Artwork by H5 — the iconic studio behind Daft Punk, Air and Vitalic — reinforces Skylax’s timeless and art-driven identity. This is not fast music, this is not algorithm music — this is music for those who still listen. Strictly for the heads. Vinyl only. No repress. Skylax Records.

Tracklist:

  • A1.Back 2 Zion (Tommorow)
  • A2.Enter the Co$mos (Fool)
  • B1.Mr. Captain Crunchhh
  • B2.O R G A S M A N I A

item.description: Label: Balihu | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: Disco , Nu Disco
item.content:encoded:

Just over 30 years after it first started appearing in New York record stores, one of Daniel Wang's most beloved early EPs gets a remastered reissue. Created at a point when he was still learning his craft as a producer (he owned little more than a sampler and a couple of basic synths), the six tracks combined his deep-rooted love of disco culture with nods to the tactile deep house warmth of Pal Joey, the Burrell Brothers, and the organ-rich garage-house sounds of New Jersey dons the Basement Boys. Deep, sample-rich, tactile, melodious and evocative, some of its synth-heavy tracks sound like blueprints for what became the nu-disco sound of fellow New York residents Metro Area. More than that, it remains a genuinely brilliant six-track missive that has undoubtedly stood the test of time.

item.description: Label: Pacific Coast House | Prix: 22,00 € | Style: House , Tech House
item.content:encoded:

Sam Robson continues to reissue gems from the vaults of his initially short-lived Pacific Coast House Recordings imprint, which released a string of superb West Coast house singles between 1999 and 2003. This split 12" originally landed way back in 2001 and has become something of an in-demand rarity in recent years. The now-familiar Teflon Dons handle side A, wrapping jaunty, spaced-out stabs, intergalactic pads, echo-laden vocal snippets and TB-303 style moody electronics around a hybrid acid house/tech-house groove on the swirling and immersive early morning delights of 'Vice'. Over on side B, Robson dons his The Coastal Commission guise for a deeper, dub-flecked and breakbeat-enhanced house workout that adds cosmic spoken word snippets and effects-laden ambient chords to the San Fran deep house template drawn up by Dubtribe Soundsystem and Charles Webster.

House MasterpieceSome 30 years after they first met in the DJ booth of Tokyo’s Spacelab Yellow nightclub, close friends François Kevorkian and Dimitri From Paris have finally joined forces in the studio. The result is The Nassau Excursion, a dazzlingly good three-track EP inspired by their joint love of disco and boogie-era dance records made at Island Records’ Compass Point Studio in the Bahamas. Across three essential tracks, François and Dimitri explore and celebrate this distinctive Caribbean post-disco sound – one where weighty basslines and heavy drum machine beats rub shoulders with early ‘80s synths, dub-style production, heady hand percussion patterns and arrangements drenched in space echo and tape delay.[info sheet from distr.]

item.description: Label: Environ | Prix: 22,00 € | Style: Deep Techno

To mark the passing of three decades since he established the now iconic Environ imprint, Morgan Geist has decided to reissue the label's long-deleted debut 12" - a solo EP that was just his second release. At the time, Geist had yet to develop the disco-leaning but naturally synth-heavy trademark sound he's become renowned for. Instead, he was investigating the stargazing potential of Detroit-influenced techno and jacking-but-spacey house. Check first the lightly bleep techno influenced excellence of 'Sands' and the more driving, upbeat and jacking 'Airpour', before diving deeply into the percussively rich deep techno wonder of 'Smear'. To complete the package, we get a suitably cosmic, pitched down ambient techno revision of the same track by The Connection Machine - back then a duo who had just released a fine EP on Planet E.
